<Rep. Mark Takano>: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Supply Chain Modernization (SCM) effort faces significant challenges. Without intentional and consistent effort to address these systemic issues, VA will be unable to implement a modern, enterprise-wide supply chain and logistics system. H.R. 3494 would compound those issues by authorizing a Veterans Health Administration pilot, prior to the Department standardizing and deciding its path forward.
While H.R. 3494 seeks to legislate a piecemeal approach to supply chain management through the deployment of a pilot within the VHA, it does not address any of the systemic challenges with VA's current modernization efforts. The Government Accountability Office (GAO) has acknowledged such challenges within VA, and has pushed VA to make these adjustments prior to implementation, as it noted in testimony from an April 19, 2023, Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations legislative hearing on supply chain-related legislation:\1\
\1\House Committee on Veterans' Affairs, Legislative Hearing on H.R. 592, Department of Veterans Affairs Electronic Health Record Modernization Improvement Act; H.R. 608, To terminate the Electronic Health Record Modernization Program of the Department of Veterans Affairs; H.R. 1658, Manage VA Act; H.R. 1659, Department of Veterans Affairs IT Modernization Improvement Act; and H.R. 2499, VA Supply Chain Management System Authorization Act, 118th Cong. (Apr. 19, 2023).
In addition to an effective pilot, to ensure success,
the decision-making process leading up to the choice of
a system must be sound. In March 2021, we reported that
VA was pursuing several major supply chain initiatives
that were highly interrelated and had overlapping
timelines-- potentially leading to cascading effects in
the event of changes to initiatives or delays. We
recommended that VA develop a comprehensive supply
chain strategy to address this complexity and create an
implementation plan with key milestones. VA concurred
with the recommendation and continues work to develop
this strategy. This planned comprehensive supply chain
management strategy should drive its acquisition of a
new supply chain IT platform--not vice versa.
Despite this recommendation from GAO, VA has once again chosen to move forward with overlapping timelines and acquisitions ahead of a comprehensive supply chain strategy. An amendment offered by Representative Nikki Budzinski (D-IL) would have required the Department to initiate this pilot after it had completed efforts like developing such a strategy, creating a cost estimate and realistic implementation schedule for the modernization effort, and perform an after-action report of VA's previous failures with supply chain modernization.
The amendment from Rep. Budzinski would have also required VA to conduct an assessment on the impact that its planned reorganization and personnel losses from the Deferred Resignation Program (DRP), Voluntary Early Retirement Authority (VERA), and other natural attrition would have on its efforts to modernize this system. In previous hearings, briefings, and technical assistance, the Department has noted that such a modernization effort is highly complex and will require attention to standardize the interfaces supply chain staff utilizes. With losses from the DRP and VERA disproportionately impacting ``support staff'' like IT professionals, supply chain staff, and others, concerns regarding VA's ability to deploy a new modernization effort arise.
Additionally, VA's supply chain initiative is expected to be occurring while the Department takes on significant reorganization and modernization efforts, such as the Electronic Health Record Modernization (EHRM), the Financial Management and Business Transformation (FMBT) program, and HR modernization. Performing any one of these efforts alone would be a significant strain on VA's modernization workforce and infrastructure, prior to the historic staffing and funding cuts implemented since President Trump took office in January 2025.
Representative Delia Ramirez (D-IL) also introduced an amendment to H.R. 3494 to bar VA from contracting with any company with which a Special Government Employee (SGE) has a financial interest. As VA increasingly considers external solutions for modernization efforts like supply chain, Democratic Members are concerned by the potential conflicts of interest that may arise from SGEs, particularly those that work with the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) initiative.
Many SGEs working under DOGE at VA have been responsible for assessing thousands of existing contracts at VA to determine if they are ``wasteful'' and should be terminated. At the same time, many of these special government employees--like Elon Musk--maintain financial interests in companies that could stand to gain thousands, if not millions, of dollars from securing government contracts and partnerships.
Ensuring that there is independence within VA's contracting efforts is paramount to the many modernization engagements the Department is actively taking on. Declining to accept this amendment demonstrates a lack of interest from the Republican Members in this Committee to truly root out waste, fraud, and abuse within out government, despite repeated calls for ``accountability'' in these efforts.
Democratic Members are gravely concerned that VA's current efforts at SCM are at risk of repeating the errors of other major modernization efforts, namely poor requirements development, a lack of measures of success, and an unclear strategy and cost estimate for accomplishing this effort. It would be irresponsible to authorize this program before these issues are addressed. Democratic Members are prepared to continue working with the Majority to conduct oversight of this program at VA, prior to yet another failure of VA's modernization efforts for necessary supply chain and logistics lines.
Mark Takano,
Ranking Member.
